item.description: Here are seven WNBA playoff records Angel Reese now owns originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Angel Reese isn't intimidated by the WNBA's biggest stage, which is no surprise for anyone who watched her play at LSU. After missing the playoffs in each of his first two seasons with the Chicago Sky , Reese's arrival in Atlanta has been an ideal fit. The Dream are one win away from a WNBA championship, and Reese has been central to the team's success. With one game still remaining, Reese is finishing up a playoff run that rewrote the history books. Here's a look at the WNBA playoff records broken by Reese this fall. MORE: History of WNBA Finals winner-take-all games Angel Reese WNBA playoff records The chase for a title isn't done yet for Reese and the Dream, but she now owns these seven playoff records: Most points by a center in first playoff run Reese has the record for most points by a center in a WNBA playoff run with 185 through 11 games. The three-time All-Star is averaging 16.8 points per game in the playoffs, up slightly from her regular season mark, and she has four games of at least 20 points during Atlanta's run. Most rebounds by a player in first playoff run Already a historically productive rebounder in the regular season, it's no surprise Reese now holds the record for most rebounds by a player in her first playoff run. The length of the WNBA Finals helps, but Reese is averaging 10.9 rebounds per game to this point, giving her 120 boards through 11 games. MORE: Cathy Engelbert avoids season-defining nightmare as Dream force WNBA Finals Game 7 Most assists by a center in first playoff run Reese's game isn't one-dimensional, as she also now has the most assists of any center during her first playoff run. Reese's 30 assists pale in comparison to her 120 rebounds, but 2.7 assists per game is a high mark for a center and nearly matches her regular season average. Most steals by a player in first playoff run You would expect a guard to hold a steals record, but Reese has the most steals of any player in her first playoff run. Reese is sitting on 16 steals through 11 playoff games, highlighted by a three-steal showing in Game 3 of the Finals. Most blocks by a player in first playoff run Reese is averaging 1.6 blocks per game in these playoffs, giving her 18 total and also putting her atop the leaderboard among players participating in their first playoff run. Most 3-pointers made by a center in first playoff run No one is looking for Reese to start raining down 3s during games, as she does most of her work close to the basket, but she is capable of hitting an outside shot when needed. Reese has made 10 3-pointers during Atlanta's 11 playoff games, a record for a center on her first playoff run. item.title: Geralt who? Spurs’ Victor Wembanyama arrives at Timberwolves game in Witcher-themed Halloween costume

Victor Wembanyama has continued to lead the San Antonio Spurs in fitting fashion, and it seems as if he is intent on doing the same off the court as well. Wembanyama arrived to the Spurs’ matchup against the Minnesota Timberwolves dressed as Geralt of Rivia, the protagonist from ‘The Witcher’ fantasy series. The 7-foot-4 French superstar wore a long silver wig, a flowing black cloak and a sword strapped across his back, with the Spurs sharing footage of his arrival on X. Wembanyama’s choice reflected his longstanding interest in science fiction, fantasy books and imaginative storytelling, with The Witcher being his favorite book series. Because it feels as much like a fantasy book, epic fantasy, as a dive into human psychology, and emotions,” he recently said , per The Sporting News.. “The characters are so deep. After reading seven books, it’s like I know these characters like they’re friends or family members. It’s a great, great series. My favorite.” The Geralt costume marked Wembanyama’s third Halloween-inspired NBA arrival, following his 2023 transformation into Slender Man and his 2024 appearance as No-Face from Studio Ghibli’s Spirited Away. Regardless, the Spurs play the Timberwolves hoping to continue their resurgent run after a hat trick of wins to reach 3-2 for the season. Wemby was not the only San Antonio player participating in the celebrations, with rookie Taris Reed Jr. dressing as Jim Halpert from The Office, recreating the sitcom character’s famous three-hole-punch costume. De’Aaron Fox dressed as Buzz Lightyear alongside his wife, Recee, who portrayed Bo Peep, and their children, who completed the Toy Story family theme as Woody and Jessie. Carter Bryant also joined the festivities with a costume inspired by Ace, the character played by Wood Harris in the 2002 crime drama Paid in Full. San Antonio has opened the season with two losses but are now looking exactly like the team they looked like for much of last season. item.title: Oregon survives against No. 20 Northwestern in stunning 14-point comeback at home
item.description: Oregon survives against No. 20 Northwestern in stunning 14-point comeback at home originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dylan Raiola passed for 336 yards and three touchdowns as unranked Oregon erased a 14-point first-half deficit to upset No. 20 Northwestern 34-26 on Saturday afternoon in Jay Johnson's debut as the Ducks' lead offensive play-caller. Dakorien Moore delivered the game’s signature moment early in the fourth quarter, hauling in a 75-yard touchdown bomb from Raiola immediately after Northwestern pulled within 27-26 on a field goal. Moore finished with seven catches for 128 yards and two touchdowns. Oregon (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) mounted the comeback despite losing its top two running backs, Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill, to injuries during the contest. Reserve tailback Brandon Smith stepped in admirably, rushing for 82 yards, while tight end Jamari Johnson caught a touchdown and sealed the win with a clutch first-down conversion with 1:20 remaining. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles threw for 281 yards and rushed for 93, accounting for a touchdown both through the air and on the ground. However, Oregon’s pass rush took over down the stretch, collecting three fourth-quarter sacks to blunt the Wildcats' rally attempts. MORE: Which unbeaten FBS team will lose first? Sizing up Miami, Utah and UCLA chances to finish 12-0 Northwestern (6-2, 3-2) dominated early tempo, piling up 284 yards of total offense in the first half while scoring on four of its five possessions. The Wildcats built a 10-0 advantage midway through the opening frame when former Oregon head coach and current Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly dialed up a triple-stack formation at the line of scrimmage, freeing Griffin Wilde wide open down the middle for a 64-yard touchdown reception. Oregon managed only a pair of Gage Hurych field goals before Chiles scrambled for a 5-yard touchdown run with 1:53 left in the second quarter, extending his streak of games with a rushing score to eight and pushing Northwestern's cushion to 20-6. MORE: 5 things to watch in Week 9: Judgment Day comes for Lincoln Riley, Buckeyes QBs The Ducks captured crucial momentum with 27 seconds left in the half when Raiola dropped a 10-yard fade into the back corner of the end zone to Moore, cutting the deficit to 20-13 at intermission. An Oregon fumble near midfield early in the third quarter allowed Jackson Kleather to drill the first of his two 49-yard field goals, extending Northwestern’s lead to 23-13 before the Ducks' high-octane attack took control over the final 20 minutes. item.title: 5 takeaways from Oregon's comeback win over Northwestern
item.description: The Oregon Ducks needed this win badly. The final score read 34-26, but that doesn't fully encapsulate the sigh of relief that fans felt walking out of Autzen Stadium with a victory. For the first time in a while, there was joy once again. While their chances of grabbing a spot in the College Football Playoff are slim to none, and expectations of competing for a national championship in 2026 have faded, there is still a lot of pride in the building and a lot of things to play for. After falling behind to the Northwestern Wildcats 20-6 in the first half on a chilly Saturday afternoon in Eugene, it appears that bad was going to turn to worse for Oregon's doomed season. Instead, Lanning turned in a treat for Duck fans on Halloween. The Ducks stormed back and won, outscoring Northwestern and Chip Kelly's offense 21-6 in the final two quarters, largely breathing some life into a fanbase that has been desperately hoping to see anything from this team over the last month. While some things need to be cleaned up going forward, it was a refreshing performance, especially given the turmoil we've seen off the field in the past week, headlined by the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Here are our biggest takeaways from the game: Playmakers Make Plays The Oregon Ducks have some of the best skill-position players in the nation on offense in Eugene. One of the biggest frustrations throughout the first seven games of the season was an inability to get those guys involved in the offense and let them make a difference. But this week, with assistant quarterback coach Jay Johnson calling plays, rather than Mehringer, a change was noticeable. "Players make plays," quarterback Dylan Raiola said after the game. That's the simplest way that you could explain Oregon's offensive success on Saturday. It's not as if Johnson schemed up elaborate looks that fooled the Northwestern defense time and again; rather, Raiola trusted his teammates to make plays in big moments, and they didn't let him down. Dakorien Moore had the best game of his career, catching seven passes for 128 yards and two touchdowns — the first 100-plus-yard game of his career. He had a goal-line fade thrown his way in the 2nd quarter where he toe-tapped for the touchdown, and a 75-yard catch-and-run for a touchdown in the third quarter. Jamari Johnson only had his number called a few times, but he came up huge, hauling in the go-ahead touchdown on a corner route in the third quarter, where he beat the defender off the line. He also had the game-sealing catch on 3rd down in the fourth quarter, where an acrobatic grab kept Oregon's punt team off the field and allowed the Ducks to end the game on offense. item.title: Reus, Roberto star as LA Galaxy regain postseason foothold
item.description: Reus, Roberto star as LA Galaxy regain postseason foothold By Alex Ruiz CARSON, Calif. – Legendary German star Marco Reus answered the call when his team needed it most on Saturday afternoon, leading the LA Galaxy to a much-needed 4-1 home win over Austin FC . Reus was the main man for a Galaxy side who enjoyed plenty of strong individual performances across the field, recording three assists in LA's offensive explosion against their Texas foes. The Galaxy spent this past week needing a positive result to get closer to securing a spot in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. With Saturday’s win, the Galaxy are now back inside the playoff places, moving up to seventh in the Western Conference with 44 points. “If we take care of business next week and we go into the playoffs, not a lot of teams are going to love seeing us across from them,” head coach Greg Vanney said after the match. Stars show up Reus, who missed last week’s El Tráfico due to illness, is now up to 8g/15a in his second full season with Galaxy. “Just so much quality of vision. Obviously, the assists show the vision, the awareness, the capacity to do things,” Vanney told reporters. “As long as we’re running, Marco is going to find us." Reus was not the only star to show up on Saturday. In his return from injury, Mexican international Chucky Lozano scored the second goal of his LA career with a header into the left corner. The former Napoli forward ran to Reus to celebrate. “He has impressive quality, and I really like playing with him. I believe many players would want to play with him, and I am very happy to have the opportunity to be by his side,” Lozano said. Former FC Barcelona captain Sergi Roberto also got in on the fun, netting his first goal in Galaxy colors. The Spanish midfielder recorded an assist and scored LA’s fourth goal of the afternoon. “Let's hope everything turns out in our favor, and if we reach the playoffs, I think it's going to be a completely different story. The team looks much better training by training, match by match, and that's what matters,” said Lozano. “I really believe we’re heading in the right direction we’re improving and you can see a team that’s more level-headed and focused,” he added. More to come Despite the positive result, playoff soccer for the Galaxy isn’t fully guaranteed. The G’s will spend the rest of the weekend as spectators, awaiting results from the rest of the Western Conference. The LA Galaxy can secure their postseason spot next Saturday in a Decision Day matchup at 10th-place Real Salt Lake , who sit just two points behind LA and one point outside the Wild Card spots (7 pm ET | Apple TV ). item.title: Penn State's players of the game from win over Purdue
item.description: In what has already felt like a bit of a wasted season, Penn State needed to come out of the bye week with some reason to feel optimistic about the future. So it was good to see a couple of Penn State's younger players on each side of the ball have solid outings in a 34-17 victory over Purdue in Week 9. Here are two young rising stars who helped Penn State to a victory on Week 9 against Purdue . Offense: Cam Wallace, Penn State running back How could the offensive player of the game not be running back Cam Wallace? Wallace led all players with a career-high 135 rushing yards. Wallace also scored a rushing touchdown. His rushing yardage would have been good for the fourth-most rushing yards as a team for Penn State this season. For an offensive attack that has had the running game under a microscope for much of the season, Wallace may have made a case for more playing time for the remaining four games this regular season. Wallace averaged 6.1 yards per carry, which was boosted by a 48-yard run that turned out to be the longest play of the day for either team. Wallace had 22 rushing attempts in the game while splitting rushing duties with Carson Hansen (who also had a nice outing with 96 rushing yards and a touchdown). Defense: Josiah Zayas, Penn State cornerback Freshman cornerback Josiah Zayas led Penn State's defensive effort with a team-high 5 tackles, including 3 solo tackles to lead the Nittany Lions . Zayas had 0.5 TFL in his count as well, while also helping to play a role in preventing the Purdue passing game from stretching the field with much consistency. Zayas only gave up one big play in the game on a 24-yard pass from Ryan Browne to Asaad Waseem on a 4th-and-9 coming out of a timeout, but Penn State had the game fairly under control by that point in the fourth quarter. item.title: ‘College GameDay’ staying in Indiana for Notre Dame-Miami in South Bend
item.description: Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect After two consecutive weeks in the scary state of Utah, College GameDay is staying put in Pat McAfee’s homebase for an extended stint in Indiana. ESPN’s flagship college football show announced Saturday that it’s heading to South Bend next week before the huge showdown between No. 5 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami, which will air on NBC and Peacock. That marks the second straight week in the Hoosier State after GameDay touched down in Bloomington this weekend before Indiana-Minnesota. WE’RE HEADING TO SOUTH BEND FOR ONE OF THE GAMES OF THE YEAR See you next Saturday at 9 AM ET for Miami-Notre Dame https://t.co/teaNLzggg5 — College GameDay (@CollegeGameDay) October 31, 2026 This marks GameDay’s 13th appearance in South Bend, including its first on-campus visit in 1993. It’s their first here since 2024, when they were on-site before a Notre Dame-Indiana matchup. It’s the 2nd time GameDay has shown up before a Notre Dame-Miami matchup. The first time was in 2017, when the two teams met in Florida. The Hurricanes won, 41-8. This year’s contest is a rematch of 2025’s iteration , which determined the last College Football Playoff at-large bid, given to the Hurricanes because of a head-to-head win despite the Fighting Irish’s ranking for much of the season. The double Indiana stops for GameDay are sure to be noticeable given the drama that came out of the show’s stop in Salt Lake City . Analyst Pat McAfee was so offended by a video of students lightly mocking him that he picked against the Utes, said he hoped he never returned , and compared his situation to the Charlie Kirk assassination . item.description: INDIANAPOLIS — Few steps in the journey of a state championship are as difficult as the last. Perhaps nobody understands that right now like the Castle boys soccer program. Three trips to the final weekend over the last nine years. Three runner-up finishes. Three losses of varying degrees. The Knights believe in their heart the ultimate goal is within reach. Carroll Stadium. A result that wasn't surprising based on how the match unfolded. Still a disheartening feeling for the top-ranked team after navigating multiple hurdles to even reach the final weekend. "It’s tough winning (state)," Castle coach Spenser Negley said. "When you get to this point, you run into a quality side. Sometimes, it goes your way. Sometimes, it doesn’t. No regrets. We went out and battled and competed." There shouldn't be any regrets. item.title: NFL Punishes Two Players Over Minnesota Vikings Game
item.description: Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings got good news from the NFL. Getty The Minnesota Vikings are preparing to take on the Detroit Lions, but the NFL has some unfinished business with head coach Kevin O’Connell’s group’s Week 7 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. Fortunately for the Vikings, none of it was with them directly. The NFL announced on October 31 that it levied fines against two players from the contest: kicker Spencer Schrader and cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt. Schrader’s infraction occurred during the opening kickoff, when officials flagged him for unnecessary roughness over his tackle on Vikings returner Myles Price. The NFL fined Schrader $7,639 for “tripping,” which typically incurs fines up to $12,537 for first-time offenses. Fines can reach $18,507 for second-time offenses and beyond. Taylor-Britt’s infraction also occurred during the first quarter. Colts punter Rigoberto Sanchez booted the ball on fourth-and-3, with Taylor-Britt helping make the stop on Price. The NFL fined Taylor-Britt $7,791 for impermissible use of the helmet. While his fine was also reduced ($23,882 for first-time offenses; $47,762 for second-time), there is more to the ruling for Taylor-Britt. Use of the helmet is one of several infractions that also incur strikes against players. Three strikes in one such category will result in an automatic one-game suspension. Moreover, the strikes carry over into future seasons. Notably, neither Schrader nor Taylor-Britt drew flags for their infractions. Both fines are classic examples of the NFL acting at its own discretion when it comes to disciplinary actions, including docking players for infractions that went uncalled in real time. Players can and often do appeal fines. So, there is a chance that Schrader and/or Taylor-Britt could have theirs reduced or wiped out entirely if they pursue relief. Kevin O’Connell Has Vikings Playing Disciplined as NFL Dishes Out Punishment The Vikings have only been fined twice (Dallas Turner, $23,882 and Josh Metellus, $11,941) this regular season, both after Week 3. They were docked once more (Jermar Jefferson, $5,583) following the preseason finale. So far, O’Connell has the Vikings playing the cleanest football in the NFL through seven weeks and “Thursday Night Football” in Week 8. The Vikings have the fewest penalties against them, per The Football Database . They are on track to finish with 96 penalties called against them. That would be a big leap from last season and their best finish since the 2023 season. That was O’Connell’s second campaign as the head coach. item.title: How Long is Julian Sayin Out? Why Ohio State Injury Return Timeline is Murky
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Julian Sayin #10 of the Ohio State Buckeyes walks off the field with his arm in a sling after defeating the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty Quarterback is the most important position in sports, and the Ohio State Buckeyes entered this season with one of the best QBs in college football, Julian Sayin. That makes it clear that the last thing Ohio State needed was an injury to Sayin, but that’s exactly what happened when the Buckeyes won at Indiana on Oct. 17. Sayin didn’t finish that game. He sustained an injury to his right (throwing) arm and ended the game on the sideline in a sling. The Buckeyes turned to backup Luke Fahey that day, and it’ll likely be Fahey getting the first shot at replacing Sayin. Ohio State had a bye on Oct. 24, and they’re back in action on Halloween night at USC. Fahey could also have competition from former five-star recruit Tavien St. Clair, but the Buckeyes seem to like the moxie that Fahey brings. Regardless of how the backups perform, though, fans will be waiting for Sayin. The upside of this team likely depends on Sayin’s health. And at the moment, there’s still a lot there that’s a mystery. How Long is Julian Sayin Out? Sayin’s injury return timeline is murky. Ohio State head coach Ryan Day has used the word “indefinitely” to describe the length of Sayin’s potential absence. That word, of course, isn’t really a helpful descriptor of time. It just creates uncertainty. Maybe someone will report more details eventually that give a better idea of exactly what injury Sayin sustained and what kind of timeline goes along with that. At least heading into Saturday’s game at USC, though, there was still a lot of mystery around the indefinite Sayin absence. Why Isn’t Julian Sayin’s Injury Return Timeline Clear? It’s fair that Ohio State wouldn’t want to put more details out. They don’t want to give their future opponents the benefit of knowing what the scoop is with Sayin. They could also still be considering options. They may want to see what Fahey (or St. Clair) looks like before totally committing to the plan for recovery for Sayin. This is a Buckeyes program that wants to win a national championship every season. A healthy Sayin gave them the best chance to do that, but he’s not healthy at the moment. Sayin also has an NFL future to consider, and while it might not be at the front of his mind, it’s also something that will remain in the picture. How would a Sayin return this season, or a more cautious approach instead, impact his potential for the 2027 NFL Draft, if he chooses to go that route? There’s a lot of unknowns not just for the Ohio State fanbase but for the people inside the building, too. It’s definitely not how they would’ve drawn this season up. item.description: There’s one dynamic that really helps your team, a big favorite, beat that other woeful and underdog but game team. item.title: Carson Kvapil delivers clutch performance at Martinsville to keep championship hopes alive
item.description: By Holly Cain NASCAR Wire Service MARTINSVILLE, Va. – Carson Kvapil book-ended Saturday’s Halloween evening at Martinsville (Va.) Speedway, leading early and leading late to claim his third NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series victory of the season – and of his career – in the National Debt Relief 250. Race Results: National Debt Relief 250 at Martinsville It was clutch performance for the 23-year-old North Carolinian who won the pole position and led the most laps on the day – 121 of 250 – in the No. 1 JR Motorsports Chevrolet to keep himself very much in the championship conversation heading to Homestead-Miami Speedway next week for the season finale. Ultimately, Kvapil had to hold off his JRM teammate, Justin Allgaier, for the win taking the trophy by .434-second over Allgaier, who leaves Virginia the new championship leader by 22 points over Richard Childress Racing’s Jesse Love. Hendrick Motorsports rookie Corey Day was third joining those three drivers atop the standings and positioning themselves for a thrilling season finale to decide the title. Allgaier leads Love by 22 points with Day 23 points back and Kvapil now 31 points out. Haas Factory Team driver Sheldon Creed finished sixth at Martinsville – good enough to keep him in the championship mix. He’s ranked fifth, 42 points behind Allgaier. “It’s awesome, I knew in practice we had a very fast Chevrolet,’’’ said Kvapil, who earned his, and crew chief Rodney Childers, first Martinsville win. “Able to qualify on pole but just kinda had a rough race between the end of stage one and the end of the race there, just kept getting shuffled back. “But it just really worked out. Just super excited.
